html:
Raï is a style of popular music that grew up in and around Oran in western Algeria from the 1920s and 1930s, sung first by women singers called cheikhas in cafés and at weddings.

It mixed Bedouin song with urban styles, and its lyrics were frank about love, drink and hard lives, which shocked the pious. From the 1970s young singers, who took the title cheb, added electric guitars, synthesisers and drum machines.

In the 1980s and 1990s raï spread through North African migrants in France and around the world. Cheb Khaled's song Didi was a hit across the Middle East and India in 1992. During the civil war Islamists killed the singer Cheb Hasni in 1994. See also Algeria and France.
sum: Raï is a style of popular music that grew up in and around Oran in western Algeria from the 1920s and 1930s, sung first by women singers called cheikhas in cafés and at weddings.
